claims.evidence: GOV.UK GP/practice-staff page lists England population screening programmes; NHS pages exist for bowel, breast, cervical, AAA and diabetic eye screening.
Programme pages set eligibility by age (bowel, breast, cervical), sex (breast, AAA) or condition (diabetes).
Population screening is for healthy people without symptoms; eligible people are invited.
NHS: from July 2025 people aged 25 to 64 are invited for cervical screening every 5 years (previously 3 years for 25 to 49). Breast every 3 years is correct.
claims.newSentence: Breast screening is offered every three years, and cervical screening every five years for eligible ages.

claims.evidence: Bowel screening every 2 years; AAA invitation in the year men turn 65, most men not invited again.
If you have diabetes and are 12 or over you get a letter inviting you to diabetic eye screening; breast, bowel and AAA pages say people outside the usual ages can ask for screening.
Screening aims to find disease early in healthy people; not intended for those with symptoms.
Eligible people are automatically invited if registered with a GP practice.
Screening is not intended for people who already have symptoms.
If you have symptoms, do not wait for an invitation; contact your GP, whatever your age or screening history.
NHS bowel page: offered to people aged 50 to 74 every 2 years (first kit at 50, 52 or 54 depending on when you turned 50). Sentence gives no start age, which stays unclear across sources.
Aged 75 or over: call the bowel cancer screening helpline every 2 years to ask for the test.
Anyone registered with a GP as female is invited every 3 years between ages 50 and 71.
Once 71, invitations stop but you can still have screening every 3 years by calling your local breast screening service.
Cervical screening invitations for ages 25 to 64.
Since 1 July 2025 everyone aged 25 to 64 is invited every 5 years; the 3-year interval for 25 to 49 is outdated.
claims.newSentence: Since July 2025, people aged 25 to 64 are invited every five years.

claims.evidence: Not in a retrieved excerpt; standard definition.
Men receive a screening invitation by post when aged 64 or 65 (NHS: in the year they turn 65).
Men over 65 not yet screened can contact their local AAA screening service to request a scan.
If you have diabetes and are 12 or over you get a letter every 1 or 2 years inviting you.
NHS: invited every year, or every 2 years if the last 2 tests found no changes; two-yearly interval began October 2023, not merely planned.
claims.newSentence: Invitations come every year, or every two years if the last two screens found no changes in the eyes.

claims.evidence: A screener photographs the back of the eyes to look for retinopathy caused by diabetes (page is the Scottish programme; generic description).
If you think you should have been invited, contact your GP surgery; people outside usual ages can contact the local screening service.
GOV.UK: with symptoms contact your GP whatever your screening history. NHS 111 line is generic site signposting, no clinical claim.

notes: The author's reference URLs nhs.uk/conditions/bowel-cancer-screening/ and nhsinform.scot/healthy-living/screening/ were not returned by search; replaced with returned URLs. Bowel start age is unclear (NHS says 50 to 74 with first kit at 50, 52 or 54 depending on date; older NHS England guide says 54); the draft sentence gives no start age, so keep it that way and do not add one elsewhere (summary/keyPoints also contain none). Cervical 5-yearly change (July 2025) is the main correction; check any other place in the guide that says 3 years for cervical. The guide is publishable after the three edits; support is adequate. c17 evidence not retrieved (textbook).
